evals.prompt: In my Next.js shop (project is in the shop-grid folder), components/ProductGrid.tsx shows a spinner while /api/products loads. It's usually 1-2 s on mobile and honestly it looks cheap. Can you replace it with a proper skeleton loading state? Keep SWR, and it has to work with our dark mode (we toggle a `.dark` class on <html>).
evals.expected_output: Spinner replaced by a grid-shaped skeleton that mirrors the product cards (4:5 image, name/price row, colorway line), ideally the ripple wave effect with cards popping in by distance; global skeleton CSS with tokens mapped to the project's theme including the .dark class; SWR kept; reduced motion and accessibility handled; no new dependencies.
expectations: Spinner removed: ProductGrid no longer renders the spinner and the unused spinner CSS is deleted
SWR is still used to fetch /api/products
All TS/TSX files parse without syntax errors
Renders in the browser without runtime errors; all 8 products appear and no skeleton is left over (mocked API)
Skeleton mirrors the product card: a 4:5 image placeholder, a name/price row and a colorway line, inside the same grid layout
Skeleton colours follow dark mode via the project's .dark class (tokens redefined under .dark or derived from the theme variables)
Animations are disabled or reduced under prefers-reduced-motion
Skeleton is hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden) and the region exposes a loading state (aria-busy or role=status)
Products are revealed with a transition (cross-fade or staggered pop-in), not an instant swap
The loading effect or the reveal is staggered across the grid by item position (a wave or per-card stagger)
No new npm dependencies were added

evals.prompt: our blog post page is plain html + js, no framework (post.html / post.js / styles.css in the blog-post folder). post.js fetches the post json and fills in the page, but for about a second the article area is just empty and then everything jumps in at once. the footer literally jumps from the top of the page to the bottom. add a loading state that looks good and stops the jumping
evals.expected_output: Article-shaped skeleton (title, byline, cover image with a fixed aspect ratio, paragraph lines) rendered immediately so the footer no longer jumps; ideally the synced shimmer sweep with blocks rising in reading order; cover image given reserved dimensions; error state still works; reduced motion handled.
expectations: Footer jump fixed: with a mocked 1.2 s response, the footer starts at least half-way to its final position
Cover image space is reserved (aspect-ratio or width/height), so the image load doesn't shift layout
Error path still works: on a 500 response the error message shows and no skeleton remains visible
No runtime errors in the browser with mocked data
Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion
Skeleton is aria-hidden and the article exposes a loading state (aria-busy or role=status)
Content is revealed with a transition (fade/rise), not an instant swap
The reveal runs in reading order (top to bottom), or the shimmer is one continuous band across the page
Static chrome (site header and footer) stays real and is not turned into skeleton bones

evals.prompt: In our analytics app (React 18 + Vite, see ai-summary/src/SummaryCard.jsx) there's a 'Generate summary' button that calls our LLM endpoint. It takes 4-8 seconds and right now we just show 'Generating…' and then the whole card pops in. I want it to feel like the AI is actually building the card in front of you, something more special than a spinner. No animation libraries please.
evals.expected_output: A generation-style reveal: an animated placeholder while the request is pending (with reserved space), then the real card revealed with a build-up effect driven by its actual structure (ideally the dot wireframe build: dot field while pending, trace and scan reveal on arrival); React-safe lifecycle with cleanup; error state; reduced motion; no animation libraries.
expectations: No animation libraries added (dependencies unchanged; no framer-motion/gsap/react-spring/etc. imports)
All JS/JSX files parse without syntax errors
Renders in the browser without runtime errors; the final card shows 3 KPIs and 3 risk rows, and Regenerate works (mocked API)
The 'Generating…' text placeholder is replaced by a visual generation animation while the request is pending
Space is reserved while pending (min-height or a sized placeholder), so the card doesn't pop in from nothing
On arrival the card is revealed progressively (traced, built up, staggered or scanned), not all at once
The build-up follows the card's real structure (measures the rendered DOM or animates the actual KPI/insight/table elements)
Animation frames and timers are cleaned up on unmount and on regenerate (safe under React StrictMode)
Error state still works and stops the animation
Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion
